episode_title: 253 -💥BONUS EPISODE : He built 1inch in a weekend. What happened next?

real_qa.q: How did 1inch get created and what happened at the New York hackathon in 2019?
real_qa.r: Sergei and his business partner built the first version of 1inch over a single weekend at a hackathon in New York in 2019. Sergei did not sleep for 56 hours during the hackathon—his personal record. He caught Vitalik Buterin and Hayden Adams passing near his table, explained his idea to them, and they encouraged him to build it. Although he did not win the hackathon, he received 200 dollars from ENS for integrating their service, which covered his travel costs to Germany. Two weeks later, people started using and sharing the project, so he and his partner decided to continue developing it in their free time and on weekends.

real_qa.q: What is the liquidity problem in DeFi that 1inch's Aqua protocol aims to solve?
real_qa.r: Research conducted by 1inch with June shows that approximately 85% of concentrated liquidity across major DEXs is unused for the first half of the year—roughly 1.6 billion of 1.8 billion in trapped liquidity sitting idle. 1inch identified that liquidity in existing protocols is inefficiently utilized. Their Aqua protocol allows users to create multiple trading positions on the same assets without depositing funds into isolated smart contracts, enabling much higher liquidity utilization by reusing the same capital across different trading pairs simultaneously.

real_qa.q: What is the Aqua protocol and how does it allow liquidity reuse on 1inch?
real_qa.r: Aqua is 1inch's protocol that lets users manage complex liquidity positions on the same assets without isolating funds in individual smart contracts. For example, with 10,000 USDC, a user can create positions to buy and sell multiple assets simultaneously—such as Tesla, Apple, and Nvidia stocks—and even create positions between existing pairs to capture volume. The liquidity remains on the user's wallet, so users can still participate in governance if they hold utility tokens. This approach achieves much higher liquidity utilization than traditional isolated two-pair pools. Since launching in late July, Aqua has already exceeded 4 billion dollars in weathered loss volume.

real_qa.q: When did 1inch raise its first funding round and from which investors?
real_qa.r: 1inch's first funding round was in June 2020, led by Dragonfly Capital and Binance Labs, with additional investors including Greenfield from Germany. The funding allowed Sergei to move into a proper apartment and hire more team members to share responsibilities. The team was already oversubscribed in this first round, and approximately three to four months later, they raised a second round of around 170 million US dollars to build institutional-grade protocols and infrastructure.

real_qa.q: What percentage of RWA trading volume does 1inch currently represent, and which major institutions use 1inch infrastructure?
real_qa.r: 1inch currently handles approximately 60 to 70 percent of RWA (Real-World Asset) trading volume. The protocol serves as an infrastructure provider for major institutions including Coinbase, Ledger, MetaMask, and Binance. 1inch has been providing routing for swaps for seven years and is very well utilized by all these integrators.

real_qa.q: What incentive program has 1inch launched for Aqua liquidity providers?
real_qa.r: 1inch launched an incentive program with the 1inch DAO providing 500,000 USDC and the 1inch Foundation providing a significant amount of 1INCH tokens to liquidity providers on Aqua. Current incentive conditions are based on trading volumes. According to Sergei, there is discussion in the DAO community about changing the program to incentivize liquidity providers based on earnings fees rather than volume, with the next round of voting and additional incentives expected to start at the end of the current month.

guest.bio_context: Sergei is a software engineer who initially worked as a securities engineer at Porsche. He built the first version of 1inch during a hackathon in New York in 2019 after staying awake for 56 hours, then continued developing it part-time over more than a year while working support jobs and living in a mining office. After raising capital from Dragonfly Capital and Binance Labs in June 2020, he scaled the team and has since led 1inch to become one of the most recognized infrastructure providers in decentralized finance, serving major institutions including Coinbase, Ledger, MetaMask, and Binance.
